sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (Azure Boards), Link GitHub commits, pull requests, branches and issues to work items
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. 'Use AB# mentions in GitHub text to link to Azure Boards work items' in 'a commit message, pull request description, or issue description'; 'Using AB#ID in a comment or in a pull request title doesn't create a link on the work item'; prerequisite: 'Connect your Azure Boards project to the GitHub repository that contains the commits, pull requests, and branches you want to link'; connecting one repository to projects in two or more Azure DevOps organizations can cause unexpected AB# linking. The page does not say whether mentions made before a repository was connected are linked afterwards; the case re-saves the descriptions to be safe (an author's step, to verify).

brief.situation: You are the DevOps engineer at Corvid Freight Software. Every production release passes a traceability gate: each pull request in it must be linked to an Azure Boards work item. Two weeks ago the billing service moved to a new GitHub repository, corvid/billing-api. Today's release gate lists 14 billing pull requests with no linked work items, although every one has AB# in its description. The release window closes at 17:00, and the auditors sample releases on Friday.
handover: The Azure Boards project Freight is connected to GitHub through the Azure Boards app; the old repository was in that connection.
Developers put AB# mentions in pull request descriptions as the team guide says.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the new repository, the Azure Boards connection, the work items and the release gate.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The release window closes at 17:00, 100 minutes after the gate failed.

writeup.question: For the record: why the pull requests were unlinked, what you changed, and how a new repository stays traced.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: corvid/billing-api was created two weeks ago and never added to the Freight project's GitHub connection; the AB# mentions in its pull request descriptions were correct but linked nothing.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: Added billing-api to the Boards app's access and the project's connection and re-saved the descriptions; the gate passed 31 of 31. Turning the gate off ships untraced changes; a mention in a title creates no link.

parts.label: Stays traced
parts.modelAnswer: Connecting the repository is part of creating one, and a weekly audit fails if an active repository is missing.

untraced.headline: Fix the link, not the gate
untraced.body: The gate was right: the new repository's mentions were not linking. Connect the repository so the trace exists.

scoring.modelReasoning: Only pull requests from the new repository are unlinked, and their descriptions contain correct AB# mentions, so the repository is the difference: it is not in the project's GitHub connection. Add it to the Azure Boards app's access and the connection, re-save the descriptions so the mentions are processed, and re-run the gate. Turning off the gate ships untraced changes; AB# in a title creates no link. Then make connecting part of creating a repository.
